intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March

experiences.name: Djemaa el-Fna Square at Dusk
experiences.description: Experience the legendary main square of Marrakech as it transforms at sunset into a spectacular open-air theatre. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, acrobats, and musicians perform while sampling freshly squeezed orange juice and traditional Moroccan street food like harira soup, msemen flatbread, and grilled merguez sausages from the famous food stalls.

experiences.name: Sahara Desert Camel Trek & Overnight Camp
experiences.description: Ride a camel into the golden Erg Chebbi dunes at sunset, arriving at a traditional Berber nomad camp for an unforgettable night under a sky blazing with stars. Enjoy a tagine dinner cooked over an open fire, listen to Gnawa drumming and music around the campfire, and wake at dawn to witness the sunrise paint the dunes in shades of amber and rose.

experiences.name: Medina Souks & Tanneries Walking Tour
experiences.description: Hire a local guide to navigate the labyrinthine medieval souks of Marrakech, exploring the ancient leather tanneries of the Chouara district where hides are still dyed using centuries-old methods. Visit the spice souk, the lantern makers, and the carpet weavers while learning about the history of trade along the trans-Saharan caravan routes that made Marrakech a legendary imperial city.
experiences.location: Northern Medina Souks & Chouara Tannery, Marrakech

experiences.name: Traditional Moroccan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a local Marrakchi family or a riad-based chef for a hands-on cooking class beginning with a guided tour of the Mellah spice market to select fresh ingredients. Learn to prepare authentic dishes including chicken bastilla, lamb tagine with preserved lemon and olives, and honey-drenched chebakia pastries, gaining deep insight into the Berber, Arab, and Andalusian culinary heritage that defines Moroccan cuisine.

experiences.name: Aït Benhaddou Kasbah & Draa Valley Exploration
experiences.description: Take a day trip to the UNESCO World Heritage ksar of Aït Benhaddou, a breathtaking fortified mud-brick village that has served as a backdrop for films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Continue through the lush Draa Valley, Morocco's longest river valley, stopping at ancient kasbahs, Berber villages, and date palm oases while a local guide shares the rich history of the Glaoui dynasty and trans-Saharan trade.
experiences.location: Aït Benhaddou & Draa Valley, Ouarzazate Province

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Take a petit taxi (negotiate fare, ~80-100 MAD) to Hotel Aday in Derb Sidi Bouloukat, located in the heart of the Medina. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest. If hungry, grab a quick snack from a nearby street stall still open late near Jemaa el-Fna square (5-10 min walk).

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport
meals.dinner: Late-night street food near Jemaa el-Fna – try a msemen (flatbread) with honey or a bowl of harira soup for 10-20 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Keep some Moroccan Dirhams (MAD) ready before leaving the airport – exchange at the airport bureau or use an ATM. Petit taxis are metered but drivers may try to negotiate at night; agree on a price beforehand. Hotel Aday is a budget riad-style guesthouse with excellent Medina access.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast at the hotel, begin exploring the Medina on foot. Start with the iconic Jemaa el-Fna square (free entry), then walk through the souks – Souk Semmarine, Souk des Épices (Spice Market), and the dyers' souk. Practice your bargaining skills but feel free to just browse. Visit the Ben Youssef Madrasa (entry ~70 MAD), one of Morocco's most stunning examples of Islamic architecture, dating to the 14th century.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Musée de Marrakech (entry ~50 MAD) housed in a beautiful 19th-century palace. Afterward, explore the nearby Almoravid Koubba (entry ~20 MAD), the oldest surviving monument in Marrakech. Stroll through the Mouassine neighborhood and admire the ornate fountains and traditional architecture. Rest your feet at a local café with a mint tea (5-10 MAD).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna at sunset to witness the square transform into a massive open-air spectacle – snake charmers, storytellers, musicians, and food stalls. Eat dinner at the famous food stalls in the square (stall numbers 1-100 area) – try grilled kefta, merguez sausages, and fresh-squeezed orange juice. Budget around 60-80 MAD for a full meal.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby café – msemen, argan oil, honey, and mint tea for 20-30 MAD
meals.lunch: Cheap local restaurant in the Medina – try a tagine or couscous set menu for 40-60 MAD at a place like Restaurant Haj Boujemaa near the souks
meals.dinner: Jemaa el-Fna food stalls – grilled meats, salads, harira soup, and fresh orange juice for 60-80 MAD total

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes – the Medina streets are uneven cobblestone. Carry a small daypack and keep valuables secure. The souks can be overwhelming; it's fine to say 'la shukran' (no thank you) to persistent vendors. Best souk hours are 9am-1pm and 3pm-7pm.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Saadian Tombs (entry ~70 MAD), a stunning 16th-century royal necropolis rediscovered in 1917. Arrive early (opens 9am) to beat crowds. Then walk to the nearby El Badi Palace ruins (entry ~70 MAD), a once-magnificent 16th-century palace now a hauntingly beautiful ruin with storks nesting on the walls. Explore the underground passages and enjoy panoramic views from the ramparts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) – visit the historic Lazama Synagogue (small donation appreciated) and browse the gold jewelry souks. Walk along the Rue Riad Zitoun el-Jedid to reach the Bahia Palace (entry ~70 MAD), a lavish 19th-century palace with intricate tilework, carved cedar ceilings, and lush gardens. Spend 1-2 hours exploring its 150+ rooms.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Kasbah neighborhood for a relaxed evening walk along the ancient city walls. Dine at a local neighborhood restaurant away from the tourist center for more authentic and affordable food. Try Restaurant Chez Lamine near the Kasbah for mechoui (slow-roasted lamb) – a Marrakech specialty at around 80-100 MAD.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or street-side café – amlou (almond-argan paste) with bread and mint tea for 20-30 MAD
meals.lunch: Snack lunch from street vendors – bissara (fava bean soup) with bread for 10-15 MAD, plus fresh-squeezed orange juice for 5 MAD
meals.dinner: Chez Lamine or similar local Kasbah restaurant – mechoui or tagine with bread and tea for 80-100 MAD

day_by_day.notes: The Saadian Tombs, El Badi Palace, and Bahia Palace can be combined into a single walking route – all are within 15 minutes of each other on foot. Consider buying a combined ticket if available. Photography is allowed in most areas. March weather should be mild and pleasant for walking.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure (6:00-7:00am) from Marrakech for the Sahara Desert. Book a budget shared minibus/CTM bus or join a budget group tour to Merzouga (Erg Chebbi dunes) – the most affordable option is a shared 3-day/2-night group tour departing from Marrakech (typically 800-1200 MAD per person including transport, basic desert camp, and some meals). The route passes through the stunning Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) in the High Atlas Mountains. Stop at Ait Ben Haddou (UNESCO World Heritage ksar) en route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Ait Ben Haddou around midday. Explore this ancient fortified village (ksar) that has appeared in films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Cross the river on stepping stones and climb to the top for panoramic views. Have lunch in the village. Continue driving through the Draa Valley, passing kasbahs, palm oases, and dramatic desert landscapes toward Ouarzazate.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Morocco') by early evening. Check into a budget guesthouse (150-200 MAD per night). Stroll through the town center, visit the Taourirt Kasbah (entry ~20 MAD if still open), and have dinner at a local restaurant. Rest early for the long drive to Merzouga tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before departure – bread, jam, and coffee for 20-30 MAD
meals.lunch: Simple tagine or sandwich at a restaurant near Ait Ben Haddou for 50-70 MAD
meals.dinner: Local restaurant in Ouarzazate – harira soup, tagine, and bread for 60-80 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Book your Sahara group tour 1-2 days in advance from agencies near Jemaa el-Fna or through your hotel. Compare prices from multiple agencies. A reputable budget tour should include: transport in a shared minibus, 1 night in a desert camp with dinner and breakfast, camel ride at sunset/sunrise, and return transport. Avoid the cheapest tours that skip Ait Ben Haddou. Bring layers – desert nights are cold in March (can drop to 5-10°C).

day_by_day.morning: Early departure from Ouarzazate continuing toward Merzouga (approximately 4-5 hours). Pass through the Dadès Valley and Todra Gorge area – dramatic limestone canyon walls rising 300m. Stop for a short walk through the gorge (free). Continue through the Tafilalet region, passing date palm oases and ancient ksour (fortified villages).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Merzouga village near the Erg Chebbi dunes by early afternoon. Check into a basic desert auberge/guesthouse (included in group tour or ~150-200 MAD independently). Rest and hydrate. In the late afternoon (around 4:00-5:00pm), mount camels for a 1-hour sunset camel trek into the Sahara dunes (included in most group tours or ~150-200 MAD independently). Watch the sunset from the top of a dune – one of Morocco's most magical experiences.
day_by_day.evening: Spend the night at a basic desert camp (bivouac) among the dunes. Enjoy a traditional Berber dinner around a campfire – tagine, couscous, and Moroccan salads. Listen to Gnawa music played by your Berber guides under an extraordinary star-filled sky. Sleep in a traditional tent or under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast in Ouarzazate – bread, olive oil, honey, and coffee for 20-30 MAD
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside stop – sandwich or tagine for 40-60 MAD
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at desert camp – usually included in group tour price; if not, budget 80-100 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Bring a headscarf or buff to protect against sand. Sunscreen and sunglasses are essential. Charge all devices before entering the desert – limited electricity at camps. The Erg Chebbi dunes reach up to 150m high. March is an excellent time to visit – not too hot (daytime 20-25°C) and not too cold at night. Bring a warm sleeping bag or ask the camp for extra blankets.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (around 6:00am) to climb the dunes and watch the sunrise over the Sahara – an unforgettable experience. Take a morning camel ride back to the village. After breakfast at the camp, explore Merzouga village on foot – visit the local market, interact with Berber families, and see the unique ecosystem where the dunes meet a seasonal lake (Dayet Srji) that attracts flamingos in spring. Begin the long return journey to Marrakech.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back through the dramatic southern Moroccan landscape. Stop at the Roses Valley (Vallée des Roses) near Kelaat M'Gouna if timing allows – in mid-March the roses may just be beginning to bloom. This valley produces much of the world's rose water. Browse local rose products (rose water, soap, oil) at very affordable prices directly from producers. Continue driving through the High Atlas.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech by late evening (approximately 9:00-10:00pm). Return to Hotel Aday. Grab a late dinner near Jemaa el-Fna or pick up street food. Rest and recover from the desert adventure.

meals.breakfast: Desert camp breakfast – bread, jam, Berber omelette, and mint tea (usually included in tour)
meals.lunch: Roadside restaurant en route – tagine or sandwich for 50-70 MAD
meals.dinner: Late-night street food near Jemaa el-Fna or a simple restaurant near the hotel for 50-70 MAD

day_by_day.notes: The return journey from Merzouga to Marrakech is approximately 9-10 hours by road. Most group tours make 2-3 stops along the way. If you feel the group tour pace is too rushed, consider spending an extra night in the desert or Ouarzazate and taking a public CTM bus back independently (cheaper but slower). Keep snacks and water for the long drive.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech. Visit the Majorelle Garden (entry ~70 MAD for garden, extra for Berber Museum) – a stunning botanical garden designed by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later owned by Yves Saint Laurent. The vivid cobalt-blue villa and exotic plants are iconic. Arrive early (opens 8am) to avoid crowds. Afterward, browse the upscale Guéliz neighborhood (Ville Nouvelle) for a change of scenery – wide boulevards, French-era architecture, and modern cafés.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Medina for last-minute souvenir shopping in the souks. Best budget buys: argan oil, spices, leather goods, Berber rugs (bargain hard), ceramic tagines, and handmade lanterns. Visit the Mellah spice market for the best prices on saffron, cumin, and ras el hanout spice blends. Enjoy a final mint tea ceremony at a traditional café. Pack your bags and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a farewell dinner at a rooftop restaurant with views over the Medina – try Café des Épices near the spice market for affordable food with atmosphere (tagine ~80-100 MAD). Head to the airport with plenty of time – take a petit taxi (80-100 MAD) or arrange airport transfer through your hotel. Depart Marrakech with incredible memories.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or a traditional Moroccan café – msemen, honey, argan oil, and mint tea for 25-35 MAD
meals.lunch: Light lunch in the Guéliz neighborhood – a modern café or sandwich shop for 50-70 MAD
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Café des Épices or similar rooftop restaurant near the souks – tagine, salad, and mint tea for 80-120 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden is one of Marrakech's most visited sites – arrive at opening time (8am) for the best experience and photos. The garden is a 20-minute walk or short taxi ride from the Medina. For souvenir shopping, the best prices are found away from the main tourist souks – explore side streets in the Mellah and Mouassine areas. Always bargain; starting price is typically 2-3x the fair price. Keep airport taxi fare in cash.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Take a pre-arranged airport transfer or petit taxi (~80–100 MAD) to Hotel Aday in the Medina. Check in, freshen up, and take a short relaxed stroll around the immediate Derb Sidi Bouloukat alleyways to get your first feel of the Medina atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack at a nearby 24-hour café or grab street food near Jemaa el-Fna square (a 10-minute walk) – try a bowl of harira soup and msemen flatbread for ~20–30 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 very light. Confirm your hotel has 24-hour reception. Exchange some currency at the airport (ATMs available). Rest well – big days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast at the hotel, head to the iconic Jemaa el-Fna square (10-min walk) to soak in the morning atmosphere. Then explore the Koutoubia Mosque gardens and exterior. Continue into the historic souks – wander through the spice souk (Rahba Kedima), leather souk, and the dyers' quarter. Hire a local guide from the square for ~150–200 MAD for a 2-hour souk tour to avoid getting lost and gain cultural context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the stunning Bahia Palace (entry ~70 MAD) – a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan architecture with ornate tilework and carved cedar ceilings. Afterward, walk to the nearby Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and explore the historic Lazama Synagogue. Stop at Place des Ferblantiers to admire the lantern craftsmen at work.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna as it transforms into a vibrant open-air spectacle – snake charmers, storytellers, musicians, and food stalls. Enjoy dinner at one of the square's open-air grill stalls or at a rooftop restaurant overlooking the action.

meals.breakfast: At Hotel Aday or a nearby café – Moroccan mint tea, msemen, honey, and amlou (argan oil dip) for ~30–50 MAD
meals.lunch: Café des Épices in Rahba Kedima square – tagine or kefta sandwich with fresh juice for ~80–120 MAD
meals.dinner: Jemaa el-Fna food stalls – grilled merguez sausages, brochettes, and snail soup for ~60–100 MAD, or sit-down at Le Marrakchi rooftop restaurant for ~150–200 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes. The souks can be overwhelming – stay calm, feel free to browse without obligation to buy. Bargaining is expected; start at 40–50% of the asking price.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Saadian Tombs (entry ~70 MAD) – a beautifully preserved 16th-century royal necropolis hidden for centuries. Then walk to the El Badi Palace ruins (entry ~70 MAD), a once-magnificent 16th-century palace now an atmospheric ruin with storks nesting on the ramparts and panoramic views from the top.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Majorelle Garden and YSL Museum (entry ~150 MAD combined) – a stunning cobalt-blue botanical garden once owned by Yves Saint Laurent, filled with exotic cacti and fountains. Afterward, explore the Gueliz neighborhood (New City) for a change of pace – browse art galleries and modern Moroccan boutiques along Avenue Mohammed V.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Moroccan hammam experience near the Medina – try Hammam Dar el-Bacha or a mid-range local hammam (~100–150 MAD for the full scrub and soap treatment). End the evening with a relaxed dinner in the Medina.

meals.breakfast: At the hotel or Café du Grand Balcon near Jemaa el-Fna – coffee, orange juice, and Moroccan pancakes for ~40–60 MAD
meals.lunch: Lunch near Majorelle Garden – Café Kif Kif or a nearby restaurant for a vegetable couscous or pastilla (pigeon pie) for ~100–150 MAD
meals.dinner: Riad Yima restaurant in the Medina – creative Moroccan cuisine in an artistic riad setting for ~150–200 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Book the Majorelle Garden online in advance as it sells out, especially in spring. The hammam is a must-do cultural experience – bring flip-flops and a change of clothes.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure (around 07:00) on a pre-booked 3-day/2-night Sahara Desert tour departing from Marrakech. The route heads southeast over the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) through the High Atlas Mountains. Stop at the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou ksar – a stunning fortified mud-brick village used in films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Explore the kasbah on foot with a local guide (~1.5 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving through the Draa Valley – a lush palm-lined oasis cutting through arid desert landscape. Stop at Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Morocco') for a brief visit to the Atlas Film Studios (entry ~60 MAD) – the largest film studios in the world. Continue toward Agdz and Zagora through dramatic desert scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at your desert camp base near Zagora or M'Hamid. Check into a mid-range desert camp with private tents. Mount camels at sunset for a 45-minute camel trek into the dunes of Erg Chigaga or Erg Lihoudi. Watch the sunset over the Sahara from the top of a sand dune – a truly unforgettable moment.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure – packed or quick café stop en route
meals.lunch: Roadside Berber restaurant near Aït Benhaddou – lamb tagine with bread and mint tea for ~80–120 MAD
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at the desert camp – harira soup, tagine, couscous, and Moroccan pastries served under the stars for ~150–200 MAD (often included in camp package)

day_by_day.notes: Book a reputable 3-day Sahara tour through your hotel or a trusted agency in Marrakech (budget ~1,500–2,500 MAD per person for transport, accommodation, and camel ride). Bring warm layers – desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C. Sunscreen and sunglasses are essential during the day.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (around 06:00) to climb the dunes and watch the sunrise paint the Sahara in gold and orange hues – one of Morocco's most magical experiences. After breakfast at camp, visit a local Berber nomad family nearby for an authentic cultural exchange and tea ceremony. Explore the surrounding desert landscape on foot or by 4x4.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the return journey toward Marrakech via a different scenic route. Pass through the Todra Gorge – dramatic 300-meter-high limestone canyon walls with a river running through. Take a 1-hour walk through the gorge floor. Continue through the Dades Valley ('Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs') with stops at photogenic mud-brick kasbahs along the route.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight stop in Boumalne Dades or Kelaat M'Gouna (Rose Valley) at a mid-range guesthouse or riad. Stroll through the small town in the evening and enjoy the peaceful contrast to Marrakech's bustle.

meals.breakfast: At the desert camp – Moroccan bread, olive oil, honey, eggs, and mint tea (included in camp package)
meals.lunch: Local restaurant at Todra Gorge – fresh trout from the river (a local specialty), salad, and bread for ~80–120 MAD
meals.dinner: At the guesthouse in Dades Valley – home-cooked Moroccan meal, often a slow-cooked lamb tagine with prunes and almonds for ~100–150 MAD

day_by_day.notes: The Todra Gorge is best visited in the afternoon when light filters dramatically between the canyon walls. If visiting in March, the Rose Valley may have early blooms – the annual Rose Festival is typically in May but the valley is beautiful year-round.

day_by_day.morning: Morning drive back toward Marrakech through the High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n'Tichka pass (if not taken on Day 4) or the Tizi n'Test pass for a different scenic route. Stop at a Berber mountain village for a short walk and tea with locals. Enjoy the dramatic mountain scenery – snow-capped peaks, terraced fields, and traditional Berber architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Marrakech by early-to-mid afternoon. Check back into Hotel Aday and freshen up. Spend the afternoon revisiting any missed spots in the Medina or exploring the Mouassine neighborhood – one of the Medina's most beautiful quarters with a 16th-century mosque, fountain, and upscale artisan boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a farewell Marrakech dinner at a traditional riad restaurant with live Gnawa music performance. Afterward, take a final evening walk through Jemaa el-Fna to soak in the atmosphere one last time.

meals.breakfast: At the guesthouse in Dades – simple Moroccan breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Roadside stop in the Atlas Mountains – Berber omelette (kefta or vegetable) with khobz bread and mint tea for ~50–80 MAD
meals.dinner: Dar Zitoun or a similar mid-range riad restaurant in the Medina – full Moroccan feast: pastilla, tagine, couscous, and bastilla au lait dessert for ~200–300 MAD

day_by_day.notes: The drive back from the desert is long (5–7 hours). Use the time to rest and enjoy the scenery. Consider booking the riad dinner in advance as popular spots fill up on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech – visit the Ben Youssef Madrasa (entry ~70 MAD), a breathtaking 14th-century Islamic college with intricate zellige tilework, carved stucco, and cedar woodwork. One of the finest examples of Moroccan-Andalusian architecture. Afterward, browse the nearby Mouassine souk for last-minute souvenirs – argan oil, leather goods, Berber rugs, spices, and handmade ceramics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, enjoy a leisurely lunch in the Medina. Visit the Musée de Marrakech (entry ~50 MAD) housed in a beautiful 19th-century palace if time allows. Pack, check out of the hotel, and arrange airport transfer (petit taxi ~80–100 MAD or pre-booked transfer).
day_by_day.evening: Depart Marrakech with memories of ancient medinas, golden dunes, mountain passes, and the warmth of Moroccan hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast at Hotel Aday or a nearby café – fresh-squeezed orange juice (Morocco is famous for it), msemen, and mint tea for ~30–50 MAD
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nomad restaurant near the Rahba Kedima souk – modern Moroccan cuisine with rooftop views for ~120–180 MAD
meals.dinner: Airport meal or early dinner before departure

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the taxi ride and airport check-in/security. Marrakech Menara Airport is about 20–25 minutes from the Medina. Declare any argan oil or food products at customs if flying internationally. Keep some MAD for tips and last-minute purchases.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Hotel Aday in the heart of the Medina. Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome mint tea and light snack prepared by the riad. Rest and settle in.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Light welcome spread at Hotel Aday upon arrival — traditional Moroccan pastries, mint tea, and seasonal fruits arranged by the riad staff

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private airport transfer in advance. Hotel Aday is located in Derb Sidi Bouloukat, deep in the Medina — a local guide or hotel representative should meet you at the airport to navigate the narrow medina lanes with your luggage. Keep Day 1 light; jet lag recovery is key.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the riad rooftop terrace. Then embark on a guided private walking tour of the Marrakech Medina — explore the iconic Djemaa el-Fna square in the morning calm before the crowds arrive, visit the 12th-century Koutoubia Mosque gardens, and stroll through the historic souks (spice souk, leather souk, lantern souk) with a knowledgeable local guide who provides cultural and historical context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the stunning Bahia Palace (19th century), a masterpiece of Moroccan craftsmanship with intricate zellij tilework, carved cedar ceilings, and lush courtyards. Follow with a visit to the nearby Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and the historic Ben Youssef Madrasa — one of the largest Islamic colleges in North Africa, featuring breathtaking Andalusian architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the rooftop of a luxury riad bar overlooking the Medina skyline and Koutoubia minaret. Dinner at La Maison Arabe — one of Marrakech's most celebrated fine-dining establishments, offering refined traditional Moroccan cuisine in an opulent 1940s riad setting. Try the lamb pastilla and slow-cooked lamb tagine with preserved lemon.

meals.breakfast: Full Moroccan breakfast at Hotel Aday rooftop — msemen flatbreads, amlou (almond-argan dip), fresh-squeezed orange juice, honey, olives, and Moroccan coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nomad Restaurant in the Medina — a chic rooftop spot with modern Moroccan cuisine; try the harira soup, kefta brochettes, and fresh-squeezed juices
meals.dinner: La Maison Arabe — refined Moroccan fine dining; multi-course tasting menu with wine pairing available

day_by_day.notes: Book La Maison Arabe dinner reservation in advance. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Medina tour. The Ben Youssef Madrasa is a short walk from the hotel — ideal for the morning circuit.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Saadian Tombs — a hidden royal necropolis dating to the 16th century, rediscovered in 1917, featuring exquisite Italian Carrara marble and intricate stucco work. Then visit the El Badi Palace ruins, once described as one of the most magnificent palaces in the world, now a hauntingly beautiful ruin with resident storks and panoramic views from the ramparts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exclusive private cooking class at a luxury riad kitchen — learn to prepare classic Moroccan dishes including tagine, couscous, and bastilla under the guidance of a master chef. This is a hands-on cultural immersion experience lasting approximately 3 hours, followed by enjoying the meal you prepared.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Djemaa el-Fna at dusk — the square transforms into a spectacular open-air theatre with storytellers, musicians, snake charmers, and food stalls. Experience the atmosphere with your guide, then dine at Le Tobsil — an intimate, candlelit riad restaurant offering a legendary fixed-price Moroccan feast with live Gnawa music.

meals.breakfast: Moroccan breakfast at Hotel Aday
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes prepared during your cooking class at the riad — a private and authentic culinary experience
meals.dinner: Le Tobsil — legendary fixed-price Moroccan banquet in a candlelit riad; multiple courses including salads, pastilla, tagine, couscous, and desserts with live music

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class and Le Tobsil well in advance — both are highly sought after. Le Tobsil does not serve alcohol but offers excellent fresh juices and mint tea. The Saadian Tombs can get busy — arrive early.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure by private luxury 4x4 vehicle toward the Sahara Desert — the journey takes approximately 8–9 hours with scenic stops. First stop: the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) through the High Atlas Mountains, with panoramic views and a stop at a Berber village for tea and local interaction.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Draa Valley — a lush palm-lined oasis stretching for miles — stopping at the ancient ksar (fortified village) of Aït Benhaddou, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of Morocco's most iconic landmarks, used as a filming location for Game of Thrones and Gladiator. Enjoy a private guided tour of the kasbah with a local historian. Continue toward Ouarzazate for a brief stop, then push on toward Merzouga and the Erg Chebbi dunes.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the edge of the Sahara near Merzouga at sunset. Mount camels for a magical golden-hour camel trek into the Erg Chebbi dunes — the tallest dunes in Morocco reaching up to 150 meters. Arrive at your exclusive luxury desert camp — a premium glamping experience with private ensuite tents, Persian rugs, and lantern lighting. Enjoy a traditional Berber dinner under a sky blazing with stars, followed by live Gnawa and Berber drum music around the campfire.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Hotel Aday before departure — packed snacks and water provided for the journey
meals.lunch: Lunch at a scenic restaurant in or near Aït Benhaddou — traditional Berber tagine and fresh bread baked in a clay oven
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber feast at the luxury desert camp — harira soup, slow-cooked lamb tagine, couscous, Moroccan salads, and fresh fruit under the stars

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day — approximately 8–9 hours total with stops. Depart by 7:00–7:30 AM. Ensure your private driver is experienced on mountain roads. The luxury desert camp should be pre-booked — recommended options include Luxury Desert Camps by Erg Chebbi Luxury Camp or similar premium operators with private ensuite tents and gourmet dining.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn for a private sunrise hike to the top of the Erg Chebbi dunes — one of the most breathtaking experiences in all of Morocco. Watch the Sahara light up in shades of gold, orange, and crimson as the sun rises over Algeria. Return to camp for a leisurely Berber breakfast. Optional: sandboarding on the dunes or a 4x4 desert excursion to visit a nomadic Berber family in their traditional tent for authentic cultural exchange.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart the desert camp and drive to the Ziz Valley and Todra Gorge — a spectacular canyon with 300-meter-high rose-colored rock walls carved by the Todra River. Enjoy a private guided walk through the gorge floor, where the light creates extraordinary photographic opportunities. Continue to your overnight luxury kasbah hotel in the Draa or Dades Valley.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a luxury kasbah hotel (such as Kasbah Tamadot or similar premium property in the region). Enjoy a sunset aperitif on the terrace overlooking the valley. Dinner at the kasbah's fine restaurant featuring locally sourced ingredients and refined Moroccan-French fusion cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Berber breakfast at the desert camp — flatbreads, honey, argan oil, eggs, fresh mint tea, and dates
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by the camp or a stop at a local restaurant near Todra Gorge — fresh salads, grilled meats, and Moroccan bread
meals.dinner: Fine dining at your luxury kasbah hotel — refined Moroccan cuisine with locally sourced lamb, seasonal vegetables, and house-made pastries

day_by_day.notes: Set an alarm for 5:30 AM for the sunrise dune climb — it is absolutely worth it. Bring a warm layer as desert nights and early mornings are cold in March. Todra Gorge is most dramatically lit in the late morning and early afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure at the kasbah — optional yoga or hammam spa treatment. Then depart on the scenic return journey toward Marrakech via the Dades Valley (Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs) — a stunning drive through rose-growing villages (the region supplies most of the world's rose water). Stop at the village of Kelaat M'Gouna, famous for its rose festival, and visit a local rose water distillery for a private tour and tasting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the drive back through the High Atlas via a different scenic route. Stop at a traditional Berber cooperative to see argan oil production and purchase premium artisanal products directly from the source. Arrive back in Marrakech by late afternoon. Check back in to Hotel Aday and refresh with a hammam treatment at a nearby luxury spa (such as Les Bains de Marrakech or Hammam de la Rose).
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Marrakech — visit the Jardin Majorelle (if open for evening access) or stroll through the chic Guéliz neighborhood (the French New Town) for upscale boutique shopping. Farewell dinner at Dar Yacout — a legendary Marrakech institution set in a stunning 1001 Nights-style palace with rooftop views, live music, and an extraordinary multi-course Moroccan feast.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the luxury kasbah hotel
meals.lunch: Lunch at a scenic roadside restaurant in the Dades Valley — traditional mechoui (slow-roasted lamb) and Berber bread
meals.dinner: Dar Yacout — iconic Marrakech palace dining experience; multi-course Moroccan feast with live Andalusian music and rooftop cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Book Dar Yacout well in advance — it is one of Marrakech's most celebrated and sought-after dining experiences. The hammam treatment should also be pre-booked. The drive from the Dades Valley to Marrakech is approximately 4–5 hours — depart by 10:00 AM to arrive comfortably.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely morning in Marrakech. Visit the Jardin Majorelle — the iconic cobalt-blue garden designed by Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent, home to the Berber Museum with an extraordinary collection of Amazigh jewelry, textiles, and artifacts. Stroll through the adjacent Yves Saint Laurent Museum for world-class fashion and art exhibitions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute luxury shopping in the Medina souks — pick up premium saffron, argan oil, handwoven Berber rugs, leather goods, and silver jewelry. Visit a reputable fixed-price artisan cooperative to avoid bargaining stress and ensure quality. Return to Hotel Aday for checkout and luggage collection. Private luxury transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech. Reflect on an extraordinary week of culture, desert, history, and world-class cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast at Hotel Aday rooftop — a leisurely send-off with all the classic Moroccan morning staples
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café du Livre or Café de France near Djemaa el-Fna — light Moroccan fare and fresh juices before heading to the airport
meals.dinner: Airport dining or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Marrakech Menara Airport is approximately 15–20 minutes from the Medina by private car. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Confirm your private airport transfer the evening before. Ensure all purchased goods comply with customs regulations — particularly saffron quantities and argan oil volumes.

query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March
